family.description: This entry, previously known as DUF11, represents the CLIPPER domain, (Cross-Linked IsoPeptide Protein in the Extracellular Region) which is usually found in multiple copies in a number of archaebacterial proteins. CLIPPER domain adopts an Ig-like fold and contains a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate residues that form an intramolecular isopeptide bond [[cite:PUB00163642]]. The positions of the residues predicted to form isopeptide bonds are not universally conserved suggesting that some domains appear to lack the intramolecular isopeptide bonds. CLIPPER domains are found in proteins from Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Some have also been identified in multiple cell-surface proteins from archaea. In Methanothermobacter sp. CaT2, this domain plays a key role as a membrane-bound adhesion protein in the aggregation of CaT2 [[cite:PUB00097782]].

causal_graphs.context: Compare WT with K715A by circular dichroism during heating from 5 to 95 C in 5-C increments. Samples contain 0.36 mg/ml WT or 0.38 mg/ml mutant in 10 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM sodium fluoride, pH 7.4; 300 ul in a 1-mm cuvette. Spectra span 180-280 nm and average four repeat scans. pOPINF/BL21(DE3) constructs were purified by nickel affinity and SEC; tag removal is explicit for crystallography, not unambiguously for these aliquots.

evidence.explanation: Figure 6a/c, Results 2.4 and Methods 4.10 support the relative transition and initial folding control. Four spectral scans do not establish four independent protein preparations.
Exact reference, synthetic coding-sequence and deposited polymer comparisons locate the tested repeat; database mapping alone does not prove stability or adhesion.

edges.mechanism: The purified mutant undergoes the spectral transition at lower temperatures than WT in Figure 6a/c. Initial folded-like spectra and similar SEC behavior support a domain-level substitution effect, without establishing that loss of the isopeptide bond is its sole physical cause.
edges.subject: clipper-k715a-heating

causal_graphs.family_mapping: UniProtKB:A0A1Y3CHT7, B9T28_05395, is 2129 aa, sequence version 1. Its sequence matches InterPro; the tested PF01345 match is 712-812 within the 708-828 construct. Table S6 WT DNA translates exactly to that 121-aa segment; mutant DNA differs only at K715A. Deposited 9IFR polymer is GP plus the same WT segment. Other repeats do not inherit the assay.
causal_graphs.limitations: Both starting spectra resemble folded beta-sheet proteins, but the comparison does not isolate a single atomic cause. The source reports a K715-N806 isopeptide bond; local mutation effects and the C818/C821 disulfide are not separately excluded. Main text/Figure 5 say Asp748, whereas both reference and synthetic sequences encode N748/D749. Methods also say K517A in places despite Table S6 confirming K715A. No catalytic microstep, fitted thermodynamic melting constant, force resistance or native adhesion is asserted.

causal_graphs.context: After heating to 95 C, cool to 5 C in 5-C increments. CD uses 10 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM sodium fluoride, pH 7.4, with WT 0.36 mg/ml and K715A 0.38 mg/ml; four repeat scans per spectrum. The 203-nm trace and full spectra are interpreted relative to each preparation's initial spectrum.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected cooling spectra and 203-nm traces support reduced recovery. Main experimental Methods provide buffer, temperature range and averaging, but not independent-batch statistics.

edges.mechanism: Figure 6b/c shows less recovery toward the starting spectrum for the mutant than WT, including failure to regain positive ellipticity near 203 nm. This is an observed purified-domain spectral effect, not proof of a uniquely crosslink-driven microscopic refolding pathway.
edges.subject: clipper-k715a-cooling

causal_graphs.family_mapping: A0A1Y3CHT7 reference residues 708-828 contain PF01345 712-812. Table S6 independently identifies K715A as the only protein change; the K517A Methods label is inconsistent with those sequences. The crystal's GP remnant does not establish biochemical tag processing.
causal_graphs.limitations: The mutant's return toward the initial CD spectrum is incomplete, not an absence of every structural recovery. No single-molecule refolding trajectory or exclusive crosslink mechanism follows from these population spectra. Thermal dwell times, independent preparation uncertainty and raw traces remain unverified; the Asp748 versus N748/D749 discrepancy is not resolved by this assay.

causal_graphs.context: Mix 10 ul of 1 mg/ml domain preparation with 10 ul of 1 mg/ml Proteinase K in PBS, then incubate 1 h at 20, 30, 40 or 50 C before SDS-PAGE. Calculated final concentrations are 0.5 mg/ml each. PBS is 137 mM NaCl, 3 mM KCl, 10 mM Na2HPO4, 1.8 mM KH2PO4, pH 7.4. Compare matched-temperature mutant and WT lanes; separate domain-only and protease-only lanes identify the bands.

evidence.explanation: Figure 6d and Methods 4.11 support the direction and matched treatment conditions, including mixing volumes. The image does not supply independently quantified rates.

edges.mechanism: Figure 6d shows less intact mutant-domain band than WT after the matched protease incubations. The endpoint directly tests susceptibility of the purified fragment while leaving the exclusive physical contribution of its isopeptide bond unresolved.
edges.subject: clipper-k715a-with-protease

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Reference A0A1Y3CHT7 contains the tested PF01345 repeat at 712-812. The 708-828 synthetic sequences translate exactly to WT or its single K715A substitution. The full-length protein's other repeats and the archaeal MTCT_1020 system are distinct targets.
causal_graphs.limitations: The displayed gel is qualitative; no degradation-rate constant, independent replicate confidence or complete digestion is assigned. Tag status of the biochemical aliquots remains ambiguous. A substitution effect is compatible with crosslink stabilization but does not isolate it from local packing or other covalent features. No adhesion-to-proteolysis causal chain or universal family protection is inferred.

record.description: This entry, previously known as DUF11, represents the CLIPPER domain, (Cross-Linked IsoPeptide Protein in the Extracellular Region) which is usually found in multiple copies in a number of archaebacterial proteins. CLIPPER domain adopts an Ig-like fold and contains a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate residues that form an intramolecular isopeptide bond [[cite:PUB00163642]]. The positions of the residues predicted to form isopeptide bonds are not universally conserved suggesting that some domains appear to lack the intramolecular isopeptide bonds. CLIPPER domains are found in proteins from Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Some have also been identified in multiple cell-surface proteins from archaea. In Methanothermobacter sp. CaT2, this domain plays a key role as a membrane-bound adhesion protein in the aggregation of CaT2 [[cite:PUB00097782]].

evidence.explanation: Figures 5/6/S8 were visually inspected and Table S6 coding sequences translated. K715A is the only encoded protein change; N748/D749 conflicts with the proposed Asp748 label. Raw diffraction and biophysical data were not reanalyzed.

Selected CaT2 Results and Discussion distinguish whole MTCT_1020 aggregation from domain-specific DUF11 causality. Other regions or full-protein architecture remain alternative explanations; no archaeal edge is imported here.

discussions.notes: Obtain experimental clone/tag records and reconciled residue numbering; examine additional bacterial and archaeal members with their own interventions. Comparative absence of aggregation is not a universal negative. Partial scientific self-review; IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Reconcile residue labels and biochemical processing, and test transfer from a purified repeat to native CLIPPER-bearing proteins.
discussions.rationale: Table S6 and 9IFR resolve the intended fragment, but do not validate the proposed catalytic Asp748 label or every biochemical aliquot. Three measured substitution effects do not establish native adhesion, force response, bond-formation kinetics or a shared function across all repeats.
